title: Mixed request costs, uneven servers
description: Your L7 fleet sends equal numbers of requests to each healthy backend. Some requests take 5 ms, others 2 seconds, so equal counts leave a few backends overloaded. You want better balance without a globally coordinated outstanding-request counter. Which default would you choose?

options.text: Hash every request by client IP so repeat clients return to the same backend.
options.explanation: Affinity does not account for request cost and can concentrate busy clients on one backend.

options.text: Use round robin with longer backend timeouts.
options.explanation: Longer timeouts do not balance outstanding work. They may keep expensive requests occupying capacity for longer.

options.text: Pick two random healthy endpoints and choose the one with fewer locally observed outstanding requests.
options.explanation: Power of two choices adapts to uneven work using each proxy's own observations. It avoids the coordination cost of finding a fleet-wide minimum.

options.text: Open a fresh upstream connection per request and choose the backend with the fewest idle connections.
options.explanation: Idle connection counts are not a measure of active work, and discarding connection reuse adds overhead.
